articles.title: Crystal Palace v Manchester City: Premier League – live
articles.summary: Updates from 8pm kickoff (BST) at Selhurst Park Get in touch: email Michael about the game Let’s dissect those teams a little. Palace line-up in that familiar 3-4-2-1 formation, although that front three is fluid. For all Palace’s problems at centre-back, Tomiyasu, Richards and Canvot (the latter really impressed me last season) are more than dependable and Axel Disasi is on the bench. After the Arsenal game [in the Community Shield], we struggled a bit in the middle of the field. This is a league where you need strong midfielders. Marc can do this job. On the ball, he is strong, off the ball he is defensively strong, he gives balance to the team. It’s good to be versatile. Bouaddi is an unbelievable player but he is 18, he is young, from France, he needs time. Ideally we will have two players for every position. Hopefully we can get one more in, or two in. Also maybe one or two out. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Palace line-up in that familiar 3-4-2-1 formation, although that front three is fluid. For all Palace’s problems at centre-back, Tomiyasu, Richards and Canvot (the latter really impressed me last season) are more than dependable and Axel Disasi is on the bench.

No Ismaïla Sarr in the squad, with the Senegalese linked with Liverpool. What a disappointment that he is not playing. No Jean-Philippe Mateta, he is apparently injured, although it is well known he is also anchoring for a move away. Interesting that Daniel Muñoz, reportedly subject of a £22m bid from Nottingham Forest this week, is on the bench. New £21m signing from Union Saint-Gilloise, Anan Khalaili, starts at right-wing back. At least Adam Wharton is there, Palace fans!

As mentioned, Marc Guéhi continues in defensive midfield for City, alongside Elliot Anderson. Rayan Cherki starts after his impressive cameo off the bench against Bournemouth. Ayyoub Bouaddi is on the bench but there is no Jack Grealish, which surely means that he is off: Everton and Sunderland are potential destinations.

Enzo Maresca , Manchester City manager, has been speaking to Sky about his continued use of Marc Guéhi in midfield.

After the Arsenal game [in the Community Shield], we struggled a bit in the middle of the field. This is a league where you need strong midfielders. Marc can do this job. On the ball, he is strong, off the ball he is defensively strong, he gives balance to the team. It’s good to be versatile. Bouaddi is an unbelievable player but he is 18, he is young, from France, he needs time.

Ideally we will have two players for every position. Hopefully we can get one more in, or two in. Also maybe one or two out.

Crystal Palace (3-4-2-1): Henderson; Tomiyasu, Richards, Canvot; Khalaili, Kamada, Wharton, Mitchell; Nketiah, Pino; Larsen. Subs: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Lerma, McNeil, Zavier Gozo, Hughes, Guessand, Mingueza.

Manchester City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Anderson, Guehi; Foden, Cherki, Semenyo; Haaland. Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait Nouri, Vitor Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

That Palace’s Holmesdale Fanatics fan group are “stopping all organised activity” at Selhurst Park is particularly sad.

Here are some of the finest tifos by the Holmesdale Fanatics over the years.

Below is a tifo in memory of Maxi Jazz in May 2023, unveiled alongside Faithless lyrics from God Is a DJ that read “This is our church. This is where we heal our hurts”. Maxi died in December 2022 . He was a West Norwood resident, a Palace supporter and in September 2012 he became an associate director of the club.

Below: a tifo before the Conference League final against Rayo Vallecano in May.

Below: a tifo showing Joel Ward lifting the FA Cup in August 2025, a few months after the 1-0 win over Manchester City at Wembley.

Below: a 2022 tifo depicting the Crystal Palace , built for the Great Exhibition in 1851.

Below: a tifo display celebrating 100 years of Selhurst Park, in September 2024.

Below: a tifo, at the 2025 FA Cup final, depicts three Palace supporters – father Mark Wealleans and sons Nathan and Dominic – who were once seen at Old Trafford in 2011 celebrating Darren Ambrose’s sensational strike against Manchester United . After Mark died of cancer in 2017, the image became a symbol of lost loved ones for Palace fans. Nathan and Dominic were in the crowd at Wembley in 2025 and were unaware that the tifo was planned until they saw the image of themselves and their late father with their own eyes.

“I had no idea it was going to be us,” Nathan later admitted. “I thought it was going to be something to do with a player retiring this season. Then out of nowhere someone told us and then we broke down in tears as soon as we saw. It was special, it shows there’s still a real love for not just my dad, but all the loved ones who love Palace and didn’t get to see it. All of them now know we’re on the next step.”

On Thursday, the Holmesdale Fanatics released the following statement, explaining their reasons for ceasing operations:

Increasingly driven out by the sky high ticket prices, needless restrictions that are designed to strip away the dignity of supporters and relentless harassment and legal action, many young people are choosing to opt out of a game which seems determined to push them away.

We have repeatedly warned the club that likeminded fans cannot congregate at Palace in the numbers required to sustain a growing active supporter culture. The conditions are simply not there. There needs to be a drastic shift at Palace towards younger fans and a move away from a culture in which people attend the ground expecting to be entertained, towards a culture of supporters turning up to play an active role in influencing the result.

The story away from home is even more dire. In domestic away fixtures, supporters are banned from bringing materials into stadiums, coaches are regularly stopped, and fans are arrested. Away ends across the country are increasingly dominated by older fans, with the next generation failing to come through in significant numbers.

Given these conditions, we have immense pride in all the group has achieved over the past 20 years. From being at the heart of the protests that rescued the club in 2010, to securing the away ticket price cap that has saved working class people millions and supporting the club through a record breaking period, the Holmesdale Fanatics has helped write a chapter in the club’s history that many did not believe was possible.

But now is the time for us to recognise we have taken the Holmesdale Fanatics as far as it can go in the current climate. We are therefore choosing to stop all organised activity as the Holmesdale Fanatics inside the stadium. We do not take this decision lightly.

The good news for Manchester City is that despite their woeful performance in the Community Shield , their fortunate late win over Bournemouth , the ongoing transfer uncertainty , the teething problems for Enzo Maresca and new signing Elliot Anderson, the club travel to Selhurst Park to face a Crystal Palace side in even more turmoil than themselves.

In recent years, Palace’s success has been built on their cohesion. Despite the significant departures in Michael Olise, Marc Guéhi and Eberechi Eze, Palace have won the FA Cup and a European trophy and secured strong mid-table finishes despite significant departures in Michael Olise, Marc Guéhi and Eberechi Eze. Recruitment has been excellent and the fans have never wavered, always passionately supporting their team, especially at home.

Pierre Sage, only a few weeks into the new job, is already fighting fires. Jean-Philippe Mateta is injured but wants out, as does Daniel Munoz – Nottingham Forest, now managed by Oliver Glasner, reportedly tabled a £22m bid this week for the Colombian. There is a Maxence Lacroix-shaped hole at the back and a deal for his replacement, Joel Ordonez, could be called off after complications with the Club Brugge defender’s medical. Meanwhile, Holmesdale Fanatics, Palace’s ultras group, has announced that it is disbanding. In short, it’s chaos in SE25, which will be music to City’s ears.

articles.title: Warwickshire v Nottinghamshire, Essex v Surrey, and more: county cricket, day two – live
articles.summary: Updates from the latest round of Championship matches Day one roundup | Sign up for the Spin | Mail Tanya There is play at last at the big beast bash at Edgbast on, but it isn’t going so well for Notts, who are 19 for 2 after losing Hameed and McCann for ducks. As that man Ben Sanderson spoils the dream with a nipbacker into the pads. Kent 170 for one. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Time to go and stretch my legs by the North Sea, if the rain holds off. Thanks for your company today, have a lovely evening.

Bad light at Edgbaston, where a stylish 131 not out from the in-touch Joe Clarke has carried Notts to 253-6.

Time now for me t o write up for second edition at a very damp Scarborough. BTL remains open for tea and chat.

It’s Simon Harmer with the breakthrough at Chelmsford, Dom Sibley can’t believe what he’s done, turning Tom Westley to short leg. Surrey 33-1.

Nineteen overs, two wickets. Glamorgan tootled to 149-9, 13 behind Hampshire .

Time for Ryan Higgins to take two wickets but not much more. Derbyshire 79 for three.

Hmmm, Lancs might finish today in a happy place. The last two wickets added 65 – Bailey 34, Walkden 26 – to finish a relatively perky 180 all out. And Worcestershire are now 0-1, Lategan caught off Bailey for 0.

Somerset have lost their first second-innings wicket, Josh Thomas for 48, edging to slip. Somerset 94-1, a lead of 46.

Essex were all out with a lead of 96, with six wickets for Rahul Chahar. Burns and Sibley aren’t picking their toenails in the second innings – already 29-0.

It’s been raining again here at Scarborough and there was time only for Leicestershire to reach 12-0 before a combination of bad light and gloom sent the players scurrying away. There are still a handful of spectators braving it out though.

Time for me to write u p for Friday first edition, will be back soon but in the meantime do chat on BTL.

Dom Bess and George Hil l had been swinging with lusty seaside abandon here at Scarborough, but Bess went one time too many and is caught at backward point. A second wicket for Hull whose speed and bounce has been a useful point of difference as the commentators love to say. Yorks 202-7.

After losing 8 for 96 this morning, Kent’s ninth wicket partnership added a precious 80. Daniel Bell-Drummond is still unbeaten on 61, Milnes just out for 37. Kent 336-9

Don’t be too jealous but Ali Martin has spent this summer locked away with Chris Woakes in cafes, pubs and over the kitchen table, winkling out the real Woakes story. In Ali’s words, “he was impossibly engaged with the whole project and so the reader can be guaranteed it is very much his story, in his words. Packed with behind the scenes details, dressing room tales, the highs, the lows, the greats he played with and against.” Sounds brilliant and you can preorder it here .

To Edgbaston, where things are nip and tuck/knit and pearl. Notts 148 for five, with Clarke still there on 65. Wickets for Mousley, Hannon-Dalby, Bamber and Barnard – no Woakes for Warwicks this round.

Precious runs from Dan Douthwaite and Timm van der Gugten at Sophia Gardens– rhwie ninth-wicket partnership of 27 has taken Glamorgan to within 16 of Hampshire . It looks as if Glamorgan will be in another one-innings shoot-out.

If you haven’t read this already, much sense spoken from uncles Stuart and Jimmy.

How are Essex doing? Very well thank you, with Dean Elgar’s 92 easing them to parity with Surrey with just three wickets down. Two wickets to Dan Worrall.

There were some nice quotes from Sam Cook last night after he zipped down to Chelmsford from Lord’s, and finished with three wickets.

“Training with those guys [with England], some of the best players in the world, you are obviously going to raise your game. Bowling to those guys you have to be at your best. You can definitely take confidence from bowling at people in that set-up and you try and use that when you come back and play here. It probably helped contribute to the success I had with the ball today.

“Every time I’ve been involved with England, whether that be with the Lions and the exposure I’ve had to the likes of James Anderson and Stuart Broad, I’ve really tried to pick these guys’ brains. And recently at The Hundred I’ve spent three weeks with Chris Woakes and they are three guys to try and draw experiences from. There are so many brains around it would be stupid not to try and pick up some tips from where you can. You would be silly not to tap into that amount of experience and quality and I try and do that as much as possible.”

Sussex have a six run lead at Hove, but Overton (4-56) and Gregory (3-55) are on the prowl. If John Simpson can add many more to his 34 not out, it could be a game changer.

Rain at New Road, a blessing for Lancashire who stagger up the steps 106-6.

Oooh, that’s a dismissive shot from George Hill who spanners Holland down the ground to appreciative applause from the Scarborough faithful, including those sitting by the line of pink balloons in front of the tea room.

To New Road, where Lancs are 98 for five, Rocky Flintoff dabbled a catch to slip and Arav Shetty danced and swiped. Keaton Jennings appears to have hit the accelerator in despair, with five fours and a six in his 51 not out.

And there won’t be a first century of the season for James Wharton here at North Marine Road, as he gives Tattersall his fifth catch of the match (all off different bowlers).Yorks 146 for six.

Beyond the boundary , Josh Hull reaches down 20 feet to touch his toes, and a disgruntled supporter shouts “get on with it” as the umpires lead the players out. And Hull it is with the first ball from the Trafalgar Road end, which flies harmlessly by.

Bedingham’s beautiful innings comes to an end at CLS, a nice wicket for Daz Ahmed’s scrapbook. Bedingham stood up straight and whipped Ahmed high but found the catcher not the rope.

Another one down at Hove , James Coles having a go and losing his sticks. Sussex 172-5.

At Durham , Glos are fighting back. A wicket for Killeen now, Clark for eight. Durham 229-5.

Craig Overton will drag Somerset back into this match until his boot studs are dust. He’s dismissed Clark (85) and Tear (34). Sussex 154-4 trail by 48.

Oh Lancs, now 28 for three – Bohannon (1) and Harris (4) following Hurst to early bath. Jennings and young Flintoff to barracade the door.

Forget that, the North Marine Road covers are coming back on again as spectators resplendent in Saint Catherine’s hospice purple and pink head around for lunch.

The covers are coming off at Scarborough , and there will be an inspection at 12.50. The clouds coming over the shoulder of the press box look ominous.

Gorgeous from Sai Kishore. Stokes throws his bat up in tumbling frustration as Kishore slide infront of the umpire and floats one through bat and pad. Stokes out for 45, seven fours and a six. Durham 194-4.

A high elbow, a single, and that’s 100 from 99 balls! His fifth of the CC season. What a player.

The skies are filthy at CLS, the floodlights on. Bedingham is still in the nineties, though hardly marooned, with 99 off 97 balls.

No Moores, no Stanley, no Anderson for Lancashire, who were invited to bat by Worcestershire and are already stumbling, boots on the wrong foot. Hurst caught off Taylor for 2.

Gloucestershire haven’t had any luck changing the ball at CLS so must take their punishement. An on-song Bedingham (97) and a punchy Ben Stokes (33) equals 180-3 and counting.

“Seeing as you don’t seem likely to be watching much cricket for a while at Scarbados - the Met Office is showing more showers coming to add to all of the early morning rain - I thought it was time to look at Surrey’s season. ”The usual caveat applies that we should see how the Essex reply pans out before we declare them in crisis, but what had skipped my attention was the extent that Nottinghamshire have donned the black stiletto boots, strapped on the latex corset, grabbed a bullwhip and treated Surrey like their gimp.

“It’s not just eviscerating them in last week’s County Championship , although, given everything else that has passed at The Oval in the competition this season, bowling them out for 162 and 183 was like stubbing a cigarette out on their collective buttock. A buttock that would already have been red raw and smarting from the spanking delivered at the same venue in the final group game of the One Day Cup (by 6 wickets with two overs and a ball to spare) to end Surrey’s involvement.

“This in turn was preceded by a lick-my-boots quarter-final defeat in the Vitality Blast, by 7 runs at Trent Bridge in mid-July. No matter how much you enjoy a bit of punishment, taking all of that in the span of five or six weeks has got to hurt, hasn’t it?”

Gosh, that multiple-contest licking had passed me by. Elgar and Westley are pressing on alright this morning, Essex 44-1. And the sun is out at Scarborough, but there will be no play before lunch.

There is play at last at the big beast bash at Edgbast on, but it isn’t going so well for Notts, who are 19 for 2 after losing Hameed and McCann for ducks.

As that man Ben Sanderson spoils the dream with a nipbacker into the pads. Kent 170 for one.

Except Scarborough and Sophia Gardens, where Glamorgan were cheesed off by Sonny Baker’s spectacular entrance yesterday “It’s not really for me to comment on [the ECB rule],” said Ben Kellaway. “We just have to try forget about it but [Baker] came on fresh late in the day, getting dark and bowled nicely.

“It’s a bit frustrating and it’s a change to face a young speedster and it certainly felt like that and we unfortunately lost those two wickets to him.”

I want to eat all my breakfasts on the North Bay drinking coffee out of a cornflower blue cup, in the shadow of a ruined castle, to the rhythm of the waves. Delicious cheese scone too.

Durham coach Ryan Campbell told BBC sport last night thatBrydon Carse was mortified by events in Derby, but would play for Durham unless they were told otherwise.

“The England team are trying to restart their whole way of going about it and he feels he’s let them down,” said Campbell. “At the end of the day, he will have to live with that.”

“I’m not going to stand here and say I’ve never made a mistake but what we can do is get our arms around him and make sure he doesn’t make those mistakes again.”

“[The regulator] is going to do their job, we’re going to listen to what they say.”

“When they give us a result, we’ll act accordingly.Until then, everyone is free to play, he’s free to play for Durham, and he’ll continue to play.”

Early news from North Mari ne Road – the umpires will be inspecting at 11am and noon.

Durham ’s Brydon Carse, last pictured in handcuffs outside a Derby nightclub and subsequently dropped from England’s Test squad, took his emotions out on Gloucestershire early. He truncheoned Joe Phillips’s middle stump with his sixth ball and induced Miles Hammond into a flamboyant drive by a couple of overs later. With Matthew Potts snaffling Cameron Bancroft, Gloucestershire were on the precipice at 13 for three. A classy 60 from James Bracey enabled them to limp to 137, but Kasey Aldridge mopped up most of the rest with five for 16. Durham then lost two quick wickets, until an unbeaten half-century from David Bedingham sailed them to calmer waters.

It was another dud day for Surrey on what is turning into a miserable Championship summer. After losing the toss and being asked to bat, they were soon in trouble on a verdant Chelmsford wicket. Sam Cook, who swapped into the Essex side after being released by England, picked up three wickets alongside Zaman Akhter, as Surrey were dismissed for 183. Adam Thomas top scored with 43, but there were few consolation runs for Ollie Pope, also surplus to requirements at Lord’s. There was just time for Essex’s Paul Walter to be caught behind before bad light stopped play.

Honours were fairly even at North Marine Road where the rain blew in mid-afternoon. Leicestershire ’s Josh Davey plucked out both Yorkshire openers cheaply, but Sam Whiteman and James Wharton, unbeaten on 70, restocked the shelves. Jonny Bairstow flashed hazardly and was caught behind for one, to Scarborough sighs.

Zak Crawley’s highest score of the season gave Kent a boost on a long day waiting for the rain to stop at Wantage Road. His unbeaten 82 dominated an unbroken opening stand of 154 with Ben Compton in the promotion nose to nose against Northamptonshire .

Sonny Baker ripped up Glamorgan ’s rebuilding plans, with two wickets in his first over after being subbed into the Hampshire side. It was a typically Tiggerish entrance on a damp day designed for bowlers – 17 wickets fell, including Glamorgan’s top three all for ducks. Sussex ’s Henry Crocombe grabbed a hat-trick at Hove as Somerset lost their last five wickets for 11 runs.

Good morning from a damp Scarborough. The sky is sigh-grey and the sea furious. Today could follow in Thursday’s wet footsteps, with the Met office promising heavy rain in northern England and increasingly widespread showers elsewhere.

But don’t give up just yet, there is still much to chew over after wickets tumbled yesterday. Can Surrey fight back? Will Zak Crawley make his first red-ball hundred of the year? Have Glamorgan been Bakered? Play might start at 11am round the grounds, but we’ll be here anyway. Do join us.

After losing 8 for 96 this morning, Kent’s ninth wicket partnership added a precious 80. Daniel Bell-Drummond is still unbeaten on 61, Milnes just out for 37. Kent 336-9

Don’t be too jealous but Ali Martin has spent this summer locked away with Chris Woakes in cafes, pubs and over the kitchen table, winkling out the real Woakes story. In Ali’s words, “he was impossibly engaged with the whole project and so the reader can be guaranteed it is very much his story, in his words. Packed with behind the scenes details, dressing room tales, the highs, the lows, the greats he played with and against.” Sounds brilliant and you can preorder it here .

To Edgbaston, where things are nip and tuck/knit and pearl. Notts 148 for five, with Clarke still there on 65. Wickets for Mousley, Hannon-Dalby, Bamber and Barnard – no Woakes for Warwicks this round.

Precious runs from Dan Douthwaite and Timm van der Gugten at Sophia Gardens– rhwie ninth-wicket partnership of 27 has taken Glamorgan to within 16 of Hampshire . It looks as if Glamorgan will be in another one-innings shoot-out.
If you haven’t read this already, much sense spoken from uncles Stuart and Jimmy.
How are Essex doing? Very well thank you, with Dean Elgar’s 92 easing them to parity with Surrey with just three wickets down. Two wickets to Dan Worrall.
There were some nice quotes from Sam Cook last night after he zipped down to Chelmsford from Lord’s, and finished with three wickets.

“Training with those guys [with England], some of the best players in the world, you are obviously going to raise your game. Bowling to those guys you have to be at your best. You can definitely take confidence from bowling at people in that set-up and you try and use that when you come back and play here. It probably helped contribute to the success I had with the ball today.

“Every time I’ve been involved with England, whether that be with the Lions and the exposure I’ve had to the likes of James Anderson and Stuart Broad, I’ve really tried to pick these guys’ brains. And recently at The Hundred I’ve spent three weeks with Chris Woakes and they are three guys to try and draw experiences from. There are so many brains around it would be stupid not to try and pick up some tips from where you can. You would be silly not to tap into that amount of experience and quality and I try and do that as much as possible.”
Sussex have a six run lead at Hove, but Overton (4-56) and Gregory (3-55) are on the prowl. If John Simpson can add many more to his 34 not out, it could be a game changer.
Rain at New Road, a blessing for Lancashire who stagger up the steps 106-6.

Oooh, that’s a dismissive shot from George Hill who spanners Holland down the ground to appreciative applause from the Scarborough faithful, including those sitting by the line of pink balloons in front of the tea room.

To New Road, where Lancs are 98 for five, Rocky Flintoff dabbled a catch to slip and Arav Shetty danced and swiped. Keaton Jennings appears to have hit the accelerator in despair, with five fours and a six in his 51 not out.
And there won’t be a first century of the season for James Wharton here at North Marine Road, as he gives Tattersall his fifth catch of the match (all off different bowlers).Yorks 146 for six.

Beyond the boundary , Josh Hull reaches down 20 feet to touch his toes, and a disgruntled supporter shouts “get on with it” as the umpires lead the players out. And Hull it is with the first ball from the Trafalgar Road end, which flies harmlessly by.
Bedingham’s beautiful innings comes to an end at CLS, a nice wicket for Daz Ahmed’s scrapbook. Bedingham stood up straight and whipped Ahmed high but found the catcher not the rope.
Another one down at Hove , James Coles having a go and losing his sticks. Sussex 172-5.
At Durham , Glos are fighting back. A wicket for Killeen now, Clark for eight. Durham 229-5.
Craig Overton will drag Somerset back into this match until his boot studs are dust. He’s dismissed Clark (85) and Tear (34). Sussex 154-4 trail by 48.
Oh Lancs, now 28 for three – Bohannon (1) and Harris (4) following Hurst to early bath. Jennings and young Flintoff to barracade the door.
Forget that, the North Marine Road covers are coming back on again as spectators resplendent in Saint Catherine’s hospice purple and pink head around for lunch.
The covers are coming off at Scarborough , and there will be an inspection at 12.50. The clouds coming over the shoulder of the press box look ominous.

Gorgeous from Sai Kishore. Stokes throws his bat up in tumbling frustration as Kishore slide infront of the umpire and floats one through bat and pad. Stokes out for 45, seven fours and a six. Durham 194-4.
A high elbow, a single, and that’s 100 from 99 balls! His fifth of the CC season. What a player.
The skies are filthy at CLS, the floodlights on. Bedingham is still in the nineties, though hardly marooned, with 99 off 97 balls.
No Moores, no Stanley, no Anderson for Lancashire, who were invited to bat by Worcestershire and are already stumbling, boots on the wrong foot. Hurst caught off Taylor for 2.
Gloucestershire haven’t had any luck changing the ball at CLS so must take their punishement. An on-song Bedingham (97) and a punchy Ben Stokes (33) equals 180-3 and counting.

“Seeing as you don’t seem likely to be watching much cricket for a while at Scarbados - the Met Office is showing more showers coming to add to all of the early morning rain - I thought it was time to look at Surrey’s season. ”The usual caveat applies that we should see how the Essex reply pans out before we declare them in crisis, but what had skipped my attention was the extent that Nottinghamshire have donned the black stiletto boots, strapped on the latex corset, grabbed a bullwhip and treated Surrey like their gimp.

“It’s not just eviscerating them in last week’s County Championship , although, given everything else that has passed at The Oval in the competition this season, bowling them out for 162 and 183 was like stubbing a cigarette out on their collective buttock. A buttock that would already have been red raw and smarting from the spanking delivered at the same venue in the final group game of the One Day Cup (by 6 wickets with two overs and a ball to spare) to end Surrey’s involvement.

“This in turn was preceded by a lick-my-boots quarter-final defeat in the Vitality Blast, by 7 runs at Trent Bridge in mid-July. No matter how much you enjoy a bit of punishment, taking all of that in the span of five or six weeks has got to hurt, hasn’t it?”
Gosh, that multiple-contest licking had passed me by. Elgar and Westley are pressing on alright this morning, Essex 44-1. And the sun is out at Scarborough, but there will be no play before lunch.
There is play at last at the big beast bash at Edgbast on, but it isn’t going so well for Notts, who are 19 for 2 after losing Hameed and McCann for ducks.
As that man Ben Sanderson spoils the dream with a nipbacker into the pads. Kent 170 for one.

Except Scarborough and Sophia Gardens, where Glamorgan were cheesed off by Sonny Baker’s spectacular entrance yesterday “It’s not really for me to comment on [the ECB rule],” said Ben Kellaway. “We just have to try forget about it but [Baker] came on fresh late in the day, getting dark and bowled nicely.
“It’s a bit frustrating and it’s a change to face a young speedster and it certainly felt like that and we unfortunately lost those two wickets to him.”
I want to eat all my breakfasts on the North Bay drinking coffee out of a cornflower blue cup, in the shadow of a ruined castle, to the rhythm of the waves. Delicious cheese scone too.
Durham coach Ryan Campbell told BBC sport last night thatBrydon Carse was mortified by events in Derby, but would play for Durham unless they were told otherwise.
“The England team are trying to restart their whole way of going about it and he feels he’s let them down,” said Campbell. “At the end of the day, he will have to live with that.”
“I’m not going to stand here and say I’ve never made a mistake but what we can do is get our arms around him and make sure he doesn’t make those mistakes again.”
“[The regulator] is going to do their job, we’re going to listen to what they say.”
“When they give us a result, we’ll act accordingly.Until then, everyone is free to play, he’s free to play for Durham, and he’ll continue to play.”
Early news from North Mari ne Road – the umpires will be inspecting at 11am and noon.

Durham ’s Brydon Carse, last pictured in handcuffs outside a Derby nightclub and subsequently dropped from England’s Test squad, took his emotions out on Gloucestershire early. He truncheoned Joe Phillips’s middle stump with his sixth ball and induced Miles Hammond into a flamboyant drive by a couple of overs later. With Matthew Potts snaffling Cameron Bancroft, Gloucestershire were on the precipice at 13 for three. A classy 60 from James Bracey enabled them to limp to 137, but Kasey Aldridge mopped up most of the rest with five for 16. Durham then lost two quick wickets, until an unbeaten half-century from David Bedingham sailed them to calmer waters.

It was another dud day for Surrey on what is turning into a miserable Championship summer. After losing the toss and being asked to bat, they were soon in trouble on a verdant Chelmsford wicket. Sam Cook, who swapped into the Essex side after being released by England, picked up three wickets alongside Zaman Akhter, as Surrey were dismissed for 183. Adam Thomas top scored with 43, but there were few consolation runs for Ollie Pope, also surplus to requirements at Lord’s. There was just time for Essex’s Paul Walter to be caught behind before bad light stopped play.

Honours were fairly even at North Marine Road where the rain blew in mid-afternoon. Leicestershire ’s Josh Davey plucked out both Yorkshire openers cheaply, but Sam Whiteman and James Wharton, unbeaten on 70, restocked the shelves. Jonny Bairstow flashed hazardly and was caught behind for one, to Scarborough sighs.

Zak Crawley’s highest score of the season gave Kent a boost on a long day waiting for the rain to stop at Wantage Road. His unbeaten 82 dominated an unbroken opening stand of 154 with Ben Compton in the promotion nose to nose against Northamptonshire .

Sonny Baker ripped up Glamorgan ’s rebuilding plans, with two wickets in his first over after being subbed into the Hampshire side. It was a typically Tiggerish entrance on a damp day designed for bowlers – 17 wickets fell, including Glamorgan’s top three all for ducks. Sussex ’s Henry Crocombe grabbed a hat-trick at Hove as Somerset lost their last five wickets for 11 runs.

Good morning from a damp Scarborough. The sky is sigh-grey and the sea furious. Today could follow in Thursday’s wet footsteps, with the Met office promising heavy rain in northern England and increasingly widespread showers elsewhere.

But don’t give up just yet, there is still much to chew over after wickets tumbled yesterday. Can Surrey fight back? Will Zak Crawley make his first red-ball hundred of the year? Have Glamorgan been Bakered? Play might start at 11am round the grounds, but we’ll be here anyway. Do join us.

articles.title: I dug through hundreds of Labor Day sales to find real deals on high-quality products that last
articles.summary: Prepare for autumn with our favorite end-of-season deals on staples including leaf blowers, blankets and bedding College grads share the room essentials that weathered the dorm Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things Labor Day offers one last hurrah for summer, a chance to reset for fall, and if you’re shopping, some choice end-of-season discounts. No matter your plans for the long weekend, we found sales on products to make the most of it while helping you prepare for the colder months ahead. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Prepare for autumn with our favorite end-of-season deals on staples including leaf blowers, blankets and bedding

Labor Day offers one last hurrah for summer, a chance to reset for fall, and if you’re shopping, some choice end-of-season discounts.

No matter your plans for the long weekend, we found sales on products to make the most of it while helping you prepare for the colder months ahead.

Here are 42 of our favorite Labor Day sales, including a food storage system for stashing your leftovers and a blanket to replace your summer linens .

Our Place’s six-in-one multicooker is ideal for city dwellers with limited counter space. “If you’re deciding between a rice cooker, a slow cooker or a pressure cooker, this combines all those capabilities into one appliance,” writes Filter contributor Kiki Aranita in our roundup of the very best rice cookers . Although it wasn’t the most intuitive of the models we tested, it did whip up brown rice in an impressive 20 minutes.

We’ve recommended Caraway’s cookware for its nonstick properties and Instagram-friendly aesthetic, all in a nontoxic construction . Recently, Karen Yuan, a Filter commissioning editor, tried its new 3 qt pan , which she said produced “possibly the easiest onion saute I’ve ever done”, during testing. For a cleaner way to cook, grab Caraway’s comprehensive Clean Start Bundle , a 39-piece cookware set including ceramic pots and pans, bakeware, food storage and cutting boards for $705 off.

Anyday’s food storage earned glowing reviews in our testing for its compatibility with use in the fridge, freezer, microwave, oven and dishwasher, consolidating both cookware and storage into one handy set. From 27 August to 8 September, get up to 30% off sitewide, plus a free two-pack of two-cup glass dishes in the blueberry colorway on orders over $150.

Our Place makes pans that not only perform *chef’s kiss*, but are also free of harmful Pfas chemicals. Our testers from Drexel Food Lab crowned the Titanium Always Pan Pro king for its “combination of lightweight handling, impressive nonstick performance and genuinely useful design”, and it is now 43% off in the smaller, 8.5in model.

In our blind protein bar taste test, Barebell’s chocolate dough flavor earned first place, beating out 11 other contenders. Now, you can try its plant-based options, like this vegan caramel peanut flavor boasting 15g of protein, for up to 30% off its original price.

Le Creuset hardly needs an introduction thanks to its heirloom-level quality that withstands decades of enthusiastic cooking. “Like all Le Creuset pans, it holds heat well and distributes it evenly, and moves from stove to oven to table effortlessly,” said Julia Skinner, a Filter contributor and kitchen expert. Simmer hearty soups, stews and more for 20% off.

If your kitchen is looking a little cluttered, score a solid 20% off this cooking expert- approved air fryer that bakes, broils and roasts. It’s even a favorite around the Guardian’s newsroom: “It allowed me to sear, pressure-cook and air-fry my food without having to buy loads of extra equipment, and it was much quicker than using the oven,” writes Sammy Gecsoyler, a Guardian news reporter.

The Dyson Airwrap i.d. has become synonymous with billowing locks previously reserved for pricey salon visits, and our testing proves it deserves the rep. When reviewer Juno DeMelo pitted it against a similar model from Shark, she found it to be more convenient, better for curling and complete with a more comprehensive selection of attachments. Grab it at 20% off, its lowest-ever tracked price.

If your achy neck and back are begging for a new pillow , you can’t go wrong with this Filter favorite . For Kori Perten, a tester, the Coop Original Adjustable is the Goldilocks of sleep solutions with “its soft, memory-foam-and-microfiber embrace”, that lets you customize your preferred level of fill to suit your sleeping position.

For a quick-drying bath towel that offers “high-end minimalism”, Onsen’s waffle-textured towel does the trick, especially with its 20% sitewide discount from 27 August to 7 September. “If you’re interested in a crisp towel with a sturdy and rough-spun feel, this towel will be right up your alley,” noted Chan.

Cut down on plastic and * take great care of your hair? That can be on your 2026 bingo card for 20% off. Guardian fashion and lifestyle editor Morwenna Ferrier is a fan of this sustainable and strand-strengthening shampoo bar: “Partly because the one I use is sulphate-free, and partly because you can use it to the very end, unlike a bottle. And when you fly, it’s one less liquid to squeeze through security.”

As the air outside and in your home turns dry, so too can your airways. This cool misting option features many of the elements Chan appreciates in a humidifier: a top-fill design to reduce spills, a dimmable control panel for a more restful sleep environment and an extended run time for all-night comfort. It’s now 25% off – just in time for cold and flu season.

Got sensitive skin? Wash away the day with Kiehl’s Ultra Facial Cleanser . “The formula is fragrance-free and gently removes dirt, oil and impurities from the face without disrupting the skin barrier or stripping natural oils,” Dr Corey L Hartman, a dermatologist, said in our guide to the best facial cleansers .

There’s no jumpscare quite like the feeling of ice-cold air against your skin after a shower that’s just cocooned you in warmth. Smooth the transition to the real world with a towel bundle that Chan appreciated for its “spa-like” and dense material that glides across skin, after testing over a dozen. They are typically a splurge, but Brooklinen has discounted them 12% for a set of four from 27 August to 3 September.

An earthy, jute-style rug is a fabulous way to bring a touch of the outdoors inside or cozy up your sunroom. That’s exactly what you get with this machine-washable option, which Megan Reynolds, a contributor, describes in her rug-buying guide as having “the look of jute minus the scratchiness of the real thing”.

After testing more than 10 bath towels , seasoned product reviewer Jon Chan named these as best for gifting, on account of the wide color selection and option for monogramming. Right now they’re $15 off and you can add a monogram free of charge, making these an easy gift option if you’re getting a jump start on your holiday shopping .

Tired of waking up with an achy back ? Level up your sleeping situation with this medium-firm, pressure-relieving mattress that’s on sale until 15 September. “I have a Purple mattress. I love the darn thing; it’s not like anything you’ve ever experienced with a mattress before, you basically float on top of it,” according to the sleep entrepreneur Rockwell Shah.

When I first tested Cozy Earth’s trendy Bubble Cuddle Pillow , I was struck by how soft it was, lending both physical and visual warmth to my space. Cozy up your bedroom or add a pop of color to your couch while it’s on sale this Labor Day weekend for 20% off.

My home consists predominantly of Mrs Meyer’s cleaning products, from aromatic hand soaps to versatile multi-surface cleaner that at once cleans and imparts a fresh scent. Now that it’s 23% off, I’m eager to restock the hand soaps around my house with this 33oz refill container that’ll allow me to limit my single-use plastic consumption.

If it weren’t for my Little Green carpet cleaner , now 22% off, my house full of pets and kids would be a giant biohazard . Thanks to its impressive suction and included formula that tackle embedded and caked-on messes with aplomb, I’m rarely embarrassed about my household surfaces, from rugs to upholstery. Since buying it, I have saved hundreds on professional cleaning services.

When reviewer John Brandon put the Bissell PowerClean stick vacuum head to head against a pricier Dyson counterpart, he noticed Bissell ’s superior suction was more capable of handling dry messes, from rice to granola. Now $100 off, it’s an even smarter steal for keeping your floors guest-ready .

Upgrade your bed-rot situation with this plush blanket , which served as an uncannily similar alternative to the viral Lola blanket in testing. “The Bedsure is just as soft and warm, while costing less than half, and measuring about 10in longer,” said Chan, the Filter contributor. Nab it just in time for cuddling season for 44% off.

When we polled parents to find out about the best gifts for school-aged kids , Crayola Model Magic topped our list. “Blake enjoys creating shapes and figures using all different colors. He loves that he can let his creation air dry and put it in a display in his room,” said the parent of a four-and-a half-year-old. Now at 22% off, the white version of this modeling clay will allow them to use their imagination and fine motor skills to create artwork they can be proud of.

For Guardian beauty columnist Sali Hughes, Origins’ tinted oil-free moisturizer is a solid option if “you either can’t be bothered to apply foundation in the heat or prefer a fresher look at this time of year.” While it’s only available in one shade at Sephora, Origins’ site offers a wider range . Add it to cart for 25% off.

This hair serum impressed Sali Hughes, a Guardian beauty columnist, who praised its lemony scent and lightweight formula. “I haven’t once dried my hair without it and there’s no going back. It is – and I say this very carefully – one of the best hair products I have ever used,” she writes . Right now, you can grab it for 20% off with code JVNLOVE.

Whether you’re team carry-on or looking to tote an entire wardrobe abroad, our favorite compression packing cubes are your answer – especially when discounted by 30%. “I was able to fit another pair of joggers or a light jacket, in addition to my testing load of clothes, while saving about half an inch with compression,” said reviewer Les Shu. “For the quality and performance you get at this price, these cubes are a great value.

“When the weather makes me reluctantly switch to leggings, my go-to pair is this style from Nike. They’re constructed with a mid-weight fabric that, while thick enough to keep my legs warm, still feels breathable,” writes Filter editorial coordinator Lauren Gould in her guide to the best winter running essentials . Prepare for the colder months ahead and grab these for 33% off.

Aside from my passport, my most important travel necessity is my Monos carry-on. At once durable enough to withstand mid-flight jostling, and compressive enough to pack an obscene amount of stuff, it’s the carry-on that makes a packed day of traveling manageable. Get it for 15% off with code TRAVEL1.

Camping magically becomes “glamping” when you have got collapsible cooking gear to make a decadent bowl of noodles to enjoy under a sky full of stars. “The lid can be used like a sieve to pour out excess liquid when cooking pasta, plus these pots double up well as basins to do your washing-up in,” an experienced camper told us .

Jon Chan, a Filter contributor, is willing to bet that these socks are tougher than the ones currently in your drawer. This mighty pair withstood his rigorous testing , which included walking 150,000 steps, “poking them with a flathead screwdriver and trying to tear them apart with my bare hands”. If you do manage to destroy a pair, they will ship you a new pair for free – a claim we have tested and verified

“It’s the type of product that you buy once, quite literally with a lifetime guarantee,” Chan said.

Between its double-wall insulation to keep drinks ice-cold or piping hot, convenient carry handle and ability to withstand daily jostling, there’s not much more you could want in a reusable water bottle. Grab the white colorway – now 20% off – for your commute, workout class or someone on your holiday gifting list .

Owala, the brand behind the internet’s favorite water bottle , also makes a coffee mug that’s equally deserving of praise. It’s beloved by Filter editorial coordinator Lauren Gould for its leakproof, travel-friendly design: “Since 2024, my reliable Owala has never let me down. Finally, I don’t have to choose between spending $10 on takeaway coffee and a drenched laptop or ruined pair of pants,” she writes .

Don’t let anyone tell you it’s too late in the season to take your drinking and dining al fresco. Stay armed with your favorite iced beverages and fresh snacks with one of our favorite coolers, now a cool 25% off and its second-to-lowest price ever. “This is a sturdy cool box, easily strong enough to double as a seat if needed, and it comes with a five-year guarantee,” said tester Linda Geddes.

If noise-cancelling audio gear is not quite your jam, listen to your favorite tunes with our favorite premium open-ear earbuds for $100 off. The secret behind their superior sound quality, according to Ryan Waniata, a tester, is a “blend of Bose’s legendary physics wizardry with a novel coil frame that creates a custom clip-on grip [that] expertly targets your eardrums”.

Tune out the world and immerse yourself in your favorite playlists and podcasts with these tech editor-approved headphones. With their impressive noise cancelling properties, immersive spatial audio, generous 32-hour battery life, ability to cut distracting background noise and lightweight design, they’re a commuter or gym-goer’s dream, according to consumer technology editor Samuel Gibbs’ review .

For a fraction of the price and all the bells and whistles to keep you active and hitting your goals rain, shine or snow , you can’t beat the Garmin Forerunner 165 , which hardly ever leaves the wrist of Gould, a runner and our editorial coordinator (who owns the pricier version that lets you download music). It also earned top marks in testing by the Guardian’s consumer tech editor, Samuel Gibbs, for its high-end design and tracking metrics, making its current 20%-off deal feel extra tempting.

Brace for fall with this Filter-vetted electric leaf blower, now $70 off. When we tested seven top cordless electric leaf blowers, the Ryobi was our overall favorite for its ergonomic design and long battery life. “It is also impressively quiet. In testing, the Whisper Series produced the lowest noise levels of any comparable full-sized blower, especially at mid-range settings,” said Josh Patterson, an outdoor writer.

When the Guardian’s consumer tech editor, Samuel Gibbs, put the Venu smartwatch to the test, he noted its bright and crisp display, lightweight and stylish construction, intuitive app controls and “world-class fitness features”. Grab the latest edition of the expert-approved smartwatch for 35% off, the cheapest we’ve ever seen it.

“The Studio Pro are without doubt the best-sounding Beats headphones to date,” writes Gibbs. Music to the ears of iOS and Android users alike, these headphones, which have solid spatial audio for watching films and clear quality for making calls, are now $100 off.

“You don’t need captions; you need better speakers. And for most people, the easiest, fastest, most affordable option is a simple soundbar,” writes tech journalist Ryan Waniata, who’s been testing different models for ten years and counting.

One of our recommendations is Sonos’ Arc Ultra , an audio speaker to enhance your TV’s sound, which he says “can also be expanded with other Sonos gear for a multi-room sound or surround sound,” and is now on sale for 18% off.

Shopping for kids can feel impossible (just ask my toddler who wants nothing but also everything at the same time). Somehow, this screen-free audio player for stories and songs happens to please even the pickiest of children while also serving as a bedtime wind-down tool any frazzled parent will appreciate. Make toddler birthday or holiday shopping that much easier with this 32%-off deal.

Other pieces you might enjoy from the Filter , the Guardian’s guide to buying fewer, better things:

Biogents Mosquitaire review: the Mercedes of nontoxic mosquito eradication is worth the price

‘The perfect food storage finally exists’: I tried the new Anydeli plastic-free containers

For Kori Perten, a tester, the Coop Original Adjustable is the Goldilocks of sleep solutions with “its soft, memory-foam-and-microfiber embrace”, that lets you customize your preferred level of fill to suit your sleeping position.

For a quick-drying bath towel that offers “high-end minimalism”, Onsen’s waffle-textured towel does the trick, especially with its 20% sitewide discount from 27 August to 7 September. “If you’re interested in a crisp towel with a sturdy and rough-spun feel, this towel will be right up your alley,” noted Chan.

Cut down on plastic and * take great care of your hair? That can be on your 2026 bingo card for 20% off. Guardian fashion and lifestyle editor Morwenna Ferrier is a fan of this sustainable and strand-strengthening shampoo bar: “Partly because the one I use is sulphate-free, and partly because you can use it to the very end, unlike a bottle. As the air outside and in your home turns dry, so too can your airways. This cool misting option features many of the elements Chan appreciates in a humidifier: a top-fill design to reduce spills, a dimmable control panel for a more restful sleep environment and an extended run time for all-night comfort. It’s now 25% off – just in time for cold and flu season.

Got sensitive skin? Wash away the day with Kiehl’s Ultra Facial Cleanser . “The formula is fragrance-free and gently removes dirt, oil and impurities from the face without disrupting the skin barrier or stripping natural oils,” Dr Corey L Hartman, a dermatologist, said in our guide to the best facial cleansers .

There’s no jumpscare quite like the feeling of ice-cold air against your skin after a shower that’s just cocooned you in warmth. Smooth the transition to the real world with a towel bundle that Chan appreciated for its “spa-like” and dense material that glides across skin, after testing over a dozen. They are typically a splurge, but Brooklinen has discounted them 12% for a set of four from 27 August to 3 September.

An earthy, jute-style rug is a fabulous way to bring a touch of the outdoors inside or cozy up your sunroom. That’s exactly what you get with this machine-washable option, which Megan Reynolds, a contributor, describes in her rug-buying guide as having “the look of jute minus the scratchiness of the real thing”.

After testing more than 10 bath towels , seasoned product reviewer Jon Chan named these as best for gifting, on account of the wide color selection and option for monogramming. Right now they’re $15 off and you can add a monogram free of charge, making these an easy gift option if you’re getting a jump start on your holiday shopping .

Tired of waking up with an achy back ? Level up your sleeping situation with this medium-firm, pressure-relieving mattress that’s on sale until 15 September. “I have a Purple mattress. I love the darn thing; it’s not like anything you’ve ever experienced with a mattress before, you basically float on top of it,” according to the sleep entrepreneur Rockwell Shah.

When I first tested Cozy Earth’s trendy Bubble Cuddle Pillow , I was struck by how soft it was, lending both physical and visual warmth to my space. Cozy up your bedroom or add a pop of color to your couch while it’s on sale this Labor Day weekend for 20% off.

My home consists predominantly of Mrs Meyer’s cleaning products, from aromatic hand soaps to versatile multi-surface cleaner that at once cleans and imparts a fresh scent. Now that it’s 23% off, I’m eager to restock the hand soaps around my house with this 33oz refill container that’ll allow me to limit my single-use plastic consumption.

If it weren’t for my Little Green carpet cleaner , now 22% off, my house full of pets and kids would be a giant biohazard . Thanks to its impressive suction and included formula that tackle embedded and caked-on messes with aplomb, I’m rarely embarrassed about my household surfaces, from rugs to upholstery. Since buying it, I have saved hundreds on professional cleaning services.

When reviewer John Brandon put the Bissell PowerClean stick vacuum head to head against a pricier Dyson counterpart, he noticed Bissell ’s superior suction was more capable of handling dry messes, from rice to granola. Now $100 off, it’s an even smarter steal for keeping your floors guest-ready .

Upgrade your bed-rot situation with this plush blanket , which served as an uncannily similar alternative to the viral Lola blanket in testing. “The Bedsure is just as soft and warm, while costing less than half, and measuring about 10in longer,” said Chan, the Filter contributor. Nab it just in time for cuddling season for 44% off.

He loves that he can let his creation air dry and put it in a display in his room,” said the parent of a four-and-a half-year-old. Now at 22% off, the white version of this modeling clay will allow them to use their imagination and fine motor skills to create artwork they can be proud of.

Add it to cart for 25% off.

This hair serum impressed Sali Hughes, a Guardian beauty columnist, who praised its lemony scent and lightweight formula. “I haven’t once dried my hair without it and there’s no going back. It is – and I say this very carefully – one of the best hair products I have ever used,” she writes . Right now, you can grab it for 20% off with code JVNLOVE.

Grab the white colorway – now 20% off – for your commute, workout class or someone on your holiday gifting list .

Grab the latest edition of the expert-approved smartwatch for 35% off, the cheapest we’ve ever seen it.

Shopping for kids can feel impossible (just ask my toddler who wants nothing but also everything at the same time). Somehow, this screen-free audio player for stories and songs happens to please even the pickiest of children while also serving as a bedtime wind-down tool any frazzled parent will appreciate. Make toddler birthday or holiday shopping that much easier with this 32%-off deal.

articles.content:
The ‘dad’ look is summed up by straight lines and muted colours, while ‘dudes’ like things baggier with adornments

T here is a competition going on at the US Open this week and it’s not the one involving rackets and balls. Instead, leading men who are not entered into this year’s draw are serving looks rather than aces.

Tennis legend Roger Federer took to court on Tuesday in navy blue poloshirt and shorts, navy blue sweatbands and navy blue socks. The cuts were trim and the top was tucked in. The young Spanish player Carlos Alcaraz wore a Nike vest, untucked and the colour of Ribena, maroon shorts, and trainers that looked like a sweetshop counter.

The player’s represent two style clans that are dominating current menswear: the dads and the dudes. If you’re not sure what side of the sartorial net they’re on, here’s a quick form guide. Novak Djokovic, Taylor Fritz and Félix Auger-Aliassime are all “dads”, while Arthur Fils and Andre Agassi are “dudes”.

Away from baselines and backhands, David Beckham in his slim, sometimes three-piece suits, actor Theo James, in real life as well as in Netflix series The Gentleman, the second series of which will land next week, Idris Elba and Andy Burnham are all prime examples of “dads”.

Dudes, meanwhile, include Brad Pitt, who appears on the cover of September’s Esquire in a red shirt with hot-pink neckerchief, Adam Sandler in chaotic ensembles , and men across Britain.

The “dad” look, which has nothing to do with paternal status, is summed up by straight, tight lines, on the whole more muted colours and embellishment for practicality’s sake – a carefully placed sweatband for a tennis player, a pair of neat little cufflinks on a suit. What it is not, says men’s fashion editor Hikmat Mohammed , “is just your dad who wears normcore. It’s an elevated dad … they wear Ralph Lauren, they wear Brunello Cucinelli, they wear Loro Piana.” Or, if thousand-pound price tags aren’t in reach, they wear Cos and Arket.

Mohammed cites Mark Zuckerberg in caramel-hued cashmere on the Prada front row earlier this year as “dad”. But it’s trickled down to the latest John Lewis menswear lookbook, which is full of sensible overcoats, cashmere cardigans and Argyle knits. According to Jacqui Markham, fashion creative director, “a lot of what we’re calling ‘dad style’ is really just great menswear fundamentals rediscovered, after a few years of fashion having moved so fast in the other direction.” Searches for “elevated wardrobe staples” have increased significantly this season, she says – “polo shirts with proper collars, chinos that actually fit, the perfect cut blazer”. Plus “sales of tailoring is up 17% so far this year, making it one of our fastest-growing menswear categories right now.” In high fashion, one of the biggest recent menswear launches also offers up dad style in spades: the luxury label Toteme’s first foray into men’s clothes.

Dudes wear things baggier, have adornments for adornment’s sake – a backwards cap or a chunky chain. It’s an atmosphere that has seen the late Bill Oddie hailed a style icon . But the patron saint of the style is the aforementioned Sandler who, in 2019 was declared a fashion icon for his unapologetic “grocery-run look” by Vogue writer Liana Satenstein.

Influences on the “dude” look include Justin Bieber and his brand Skylark, which launched last year and sells baggy hoodies and baggy shorts. “It’s more street wear. It’s more relaxed, it’s more fun, it’s more colourful,” says Mohammed. “They have more camouflage. It’s, like, Chrome Hearts,” he says referring to the LA brand beloved of Timothée Chalamet (in his current iteration: a “dude”). “The ‘dude’ maybe not stoner, but they’ll take a gummy here and there.”

The rise of the so-called “schlub hub” – men who dress as slobs relative to their maximalist, often very on-social media partners – shows that neither does marital status (Bieber, who became a meme for his hoodie and Crocs, worn alongside his wife in a red evening dress , is the prime example.) While it can be about age, it’s not about age: “dudes” Pitt and Bieber are 64 and 32 respectively. Luca Guadanigno-favoured actor Drew Starkey (a “dad”) is 32. According to Ben Hewitt, brand director at men’s tailoring brand Hawes & Curtis: “The real shift towards ‘dad style’ is no longer generational, it’s about intentional dressing, whether dressing for the working week or downtime.”

It isn’t of course a binary: Harry Styles, whose 30-show run at Madison Square Garden began this week, wears “dad”-style togs but with a “dude” energy (see the cut of his suits, the billowing white shirts), plus “dude”-style togs with “dad” energy (see short-shorts with sensible loafers). JFK Jr, who recently re-dominated the zeitgeist thanks to Love Story, was both. For Hikmat Mohammed, who says he is more dude in summer, “dad” in winter: “JFK Jr out of hours was dude but when he was working that was ‘dad’.”

Why are these style camps so prevalent now? The march of the dad has been happening for a while: in 2019 the New York Times Style Magazine heralded “The Unstoppable Rise of the Zaddy,” meaning an older man with impeccable style. Mohammed thinks it could be a recession indicator: “People just want a full look that’s clear and really sharp,” he says. It is also a case of the slower menswear cycle playing out: “I feel like finally the quiet luxury that womenswear had is finally catching up to men.”

Plus, actual dads became a menswear inspiration. As the writer John Diamond wrote in The Cut this week : “Just a few years ago, there was the idea of a stereotypical dad look that usually included denim shorts, New Balance sneakers, wearing socks with sandals, and higher-rise, more-relaxed jeans. Then, in one of the oddest cases of cultural appropriation, style-conscious and young people started borrowing those looks and making them their own.”

For dudes, it helps that menswear in recent years has become more interesting in general, and men, from Colman Domingo to your colleagues, have perhaps felt more comfortable to experiment. The perfect example is Daniel Craig, known as a sharp-suited, small-c conservative dresser (“dad”), he caused a stir with a run of chaotic styling in tandem with becoming the face of Loewe, then under JW Anderson, in 2024. He became fully dude.

But who feels comfortable – and who is able – to dress like a dude is complicated. There’s a privilege to being able to present so baggily. Plus, “it’s more expensive to dress ‘dude’,” says Mohammed. Dude-style streetwear can take a lot of searching for, and can cost far more than a shirt and chinos, especially some of the rare, vintage stuff, which “[has] almost become memorabilia. It’s like having a blue chip painting in your house.” It’s not, says Mohammed, “like a grey suit [that] you can buy in Reiss or M&S.”

articles.title: 'Our parents were crossing the border an hour before the flood hit'
articles.summary: Authorities say nearly 2,000 people are missing, including more than 100 Americans and Canadians, as families await word on loved ones after the Nepal flash floods.
articles.content:
'We just want them home': Daughters of couple missing after Tibet pilgrimage

Hundreds of foreign nationals are desperately waiting to hear from loved ones thought to be caught in the deadly flash flood and mudslide along the Nepal-Tibet border.

Sisters Shreya and Ashna Ahuja are among those anxiously waiting for some news of their parents, Deepak and Madhu Ahuja, who had travelled from Texas to Mount Kailash on a group pilgrimage.

"It's only been one day, but it has felt like much longer," the sisters tell the BBC. "We just love them a lot and want them to come home." One of the siblings spoke to their parents just before the floods struck.

Nearly 2,000 people are missing, including tourists from the US, Australia, Canada, India, and the UK. Nepali authorities say more than 575 people have died.

Follow live updates: Fears of second flood as search for survivors continues

About 90 US citizens may have been impacted by the floods, the State Department said on Thursday, confirming that five Americans in Nepal have made their way to safety.

The Ahuja sisters have contacted the State Department and US embassies in Delhi, Nepal and China, but they say they have no concrete information on the whereabouts of their parents.

The region is a pilgrimage site for Hindus and Buddhists, and visited by tens of thousands of pilgrims each year.

Radhika Sharma's parents, Ramesh Sharma, 65 and Neelam Sharma, 64, two US citizens who live in New York City, were also travelling to Mount Kailash in the Kathmandu region when the disaster struck.

The pilgrimage was their first trip on their own since retiring last year.

"I am just trying to find them, I don't have any answers," Radhika Sharma told the BBC. Sharma is typically in frequent contact with her parents, often texting multiple times during the day.

"The last we know is they were at the border at 8am, so about an hour before the floods," she said. "And we are hoping that they made it to the Tibet side."

Sharma, who has been in contact with the US embassies in Beijing and Kathmandu, said: "No one has any answers."

Collapsed glacier likely caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, scientists say

'The flood took everything': Nepal survivors describe horror of loved ones being swept away

She has also connected with other Americans who are in a similar situation, to support one another and consolidate information.

At least 77 people caught in the disaster are part of a pilgrimage organised by the Isha Foundation, a non-profit group headquartered in India that also has a base in McMinnville, Tennessee.

Leslie Crespi, a community liaison for the Foundation, told the BBC that the group had been working on immigration paperwork in what was meant to be an earthquake-resistant building near the border when the water came through.

Ramesh Sharma, 65, and Neelam Sharma, 64, two US citizens from New York have been missing since the flood hit

Prabhath Sajeepa, another US citizen who went missing after the flood hit, was one of the 77 people travelling with the Isha Foundation.

Sajeepa works for a software company in California, and has been involved with the Isha Foundation for a few years, according to his niece, who lives in Germany.

"It has been terrible. I hope he is somewhere safe," his niece, Kavya Koulagi Jayatheertha, told the BBC. "We are hoping for good news."

The State Department said that the US embassy in Nepal was working closely with local tour agencies and authorities to assist affected Americans.

Officials did not provide figures or additional details regarding the Americans affected for privacy reasons.

US President Donald Trump told reporters on Thursday that his administration had offered to help the Nepalese government.

"We are sending aid and we've spoken to the leadership," Trump said. "And we let them know anything they want, we'll have."

Canada's foreign office said it was aware of 32 Canadians and permanent residents in Nepal and in the Tibet region whose whereabouts and well-being had not yet been confirmed.

"Given the extremely difficult circumstances on the ground, this number may fluctuate as new information comes in," Global Affairs Canada said in a statement on Thursday.

Canada's Secretary of State for International Development, Randeep Sarai, said on Friday afternoon his focus is on helping families get through what he can "only imagine to be a living nightmare."

According to Nepal police, more than 500 tourists are missing from 28 different countries - most of whom are foreign nationals.

The Nepal Tourism Board has broken down the missing by nationality , external .

State media in China, which controls Tibet, reported three dead and at least 558 missing there. Among these are 260 foreign nationals, CCTV said. It is not clear if these figures overlap with the numbers provided by Nepal.

Initial reports from Nepal had suggested that an earthquake may have triggered the ice avalanche and landslide.

But the US Geological Survey, which studies earthquakes, has now said that further analysis indicates "that the seismic energy was instead generated by a landslide" by itself.

Landslides or avalanches can have various triggers. One possibility is that water - either from rainfall or melting ice - may have destabilised the ground or ice.

Climate change is known to be driving faster glacier melt in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region, but scientists say it is too soon to pinpoint its role in this specific event.

The flash flooding swept away entire communities. Roads and bridges worth more than 15bn Nepalese rupees (£72.18m, $98.33m) were damaged by the floods, a government official told BBC Nepali, citing initial estimates.

Nepal's President Ram Chandra Paudel has called upon the government, political parties, social organisations, all agencies including security forces, and the general public to intensify rescue and relief efforts.

"I urge everyone to remain vigilant and actively engage in necessary coordination and cooperation in the lower coastal areas," he said.

With additional reporting by Anahita Sachdev, Gabriela Pomeroy, Helena Humphrey and Mark Poynting, climate and science journalist

Sisters Shreya and Ashna Ahuja are among those anxiously waiting for some news of their parents, Deepak and Madhu Ahuja, who had travelled from Texas to Mount Kailash on a group pilgrimage.
